chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma'il al-Marvazi in Ray narrated to us, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Marvazi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan (that is, ibn Shaqiq) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, saying: Sammak ibn Harb narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
I heard him say: 'This authority/rule will not cease until twelve Caliphs rule, all of them from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Caliphs mentioned in the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve divinely appointed leaders, serving as a primary proof for the Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt. The emphasis on Quraysh underscores the prophetic tradition of leadership remaining within the Prophet's lineage, specifically linking the twelve to the twelve Imams recognized in Twelver Shia theology.
